title: Roast parsnip and white bean dip

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain store-cupboard item; tahini and tinned beans are simple single-ingredient products.

supermarket.reason: Parsnips, cannellini beans, tahini, pumpkin seeds and the crudités are all everyday Tesco items.

basic_kitchen.reason: A roasting tray and a stick blender in a jug are ordinary kit, and the technique is simple roasting and blending.

works.reason: Roasting 500g parsnips for 30 minutes at 200°C, then blending them with beans, tahini, lemon, oil and water, gives a good dip for four, with plenty of crudités.

honest_times.reason: 20 minutes is believable for peeling, chunking, blending and cutting crudités, and the 40-minute cook time covers heating the oven plus the 30-minute roast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Roast parsnips are the body of the dip, which suits early November.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: A vegetable and bean dip with raw vegetable and apple sticks is a wholesome, appealing family snack.
